source.title: A transfer learning framework for weak to strong generalization
source.authors: Seamus Somerstep; Felipe Maia Polo; Moulinath Banerjee; Ya'acov Ritov; Mikhail Yurochkin; Yuekai Sun

page_placements.theme: Weak-label fine-tuning leaves the strong student below its own pre-fine-tuning performance or erodes its representations

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper fine-tunes strong LLMs on weak-model outputs and evaluates task performance, but does not use Burns et al.'s PGR measure. It tests the same general question using accuracy and style scores, and argues that naive fine-tuning can fail or degrade the strong model.
record.gate_note: The paper reports mathematical-reasoning results in figures and describes them in text; no exact plotted values are stated. Table 1 is flattened, but its four score columns can be assigned to the named benchmarks and metrics in order; table rows are retained separately. The gender-bias experiment uses deliberately corrupted biographies and an ask-to-improve procedure, not labels from a weaker supervisor, so it is not included as a weak-to-strong result row. The theoretical bounds concern the paper's transfer-learning setup, not the specified PGR.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes GPT-3.5-Turbo and GPT-4o-mini on 7B-and-smaller weak-model labels, as in Burns et al. Its main contribution is a specific argument that the claim needs restating. Its theory (Prop. 3.2) gives a bias floor for naive weak-label fine-tuning. The authors also redefine success as beating the un-finetuned strong model, not the weak supervisor (Sec. 6). Its Table 1 compares Burns-style bootstrapping and an auxiliary-loss proxy. The core naive-vs-weak-supervisor comparisons exist only in figures with no stated values, so V1 cannot be read from the text.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but it omits the authors' redefinition. They argue weak-to-strong generalization has only occurred if the student beats the un-finetuned strong model, not just the weak supervisor. They prove naive weak-label fine-tuning has a bias floor in their framework, and that ICL refinement provably overcomes it. Empirically, naive FT degrades the strong model, and refinement keeps content near base. GPT-4o-mini math gains are limited.
record.recipe_differences: It fine-tunes strong LLMs on weaker-model outputs, but evaluates accuracy/style rather than Burns et al.'s PGR. It also studies ICL refinement, infer-and-respond, bootstrapping, and a proxy for auxiliary loss.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with task, strong-model checkpoint, weak-label provider/quality, and training method. The paper states that persona content degradation worsens as weak-label quality decreases; GPT-4o-mini's refined math gains are limited.

fits_no_version.finding: Naive fine-tuning on weak labels lowers the strong model below its own un-finetuned performance. This holds for persona content (Figs. 1-2) and for GPT-3.5 math accuracy (Fig. 3). The degradation worsens as weak-label quality falls.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weak-label fine-tuning can degrade a strong model relative to its pre-fine-tuning capability, a comparison PGR does not make.

record.problems: The core math results are presented in plots without exact values in the text. The paper does not calculate PGR. The auxiliary confidence-loss method could not be implemented directly and is represented by a data-doubling proxy. No uncertainty estimates for the reported task scores are stated.
record.rows_left_out: No result rows omitted under the 60-row cap. The gender-bias experiment is not a weak-supervisor test: the text describes synthetic corruption of biographies and an ask-to-improve method, without a weaker model serving as the supervisor.

untested.parts: No readable comparison of the naive weak-label-trained student against the weak supervisor, and no PGR. Values are in Figs. 1-4 only.
The actual auxiliary confidence loss (only a proxy was run), ensembling of weak supervisors, and any PGR comparison.
No model-size sweep, no chess or reward-modelling tasks, no representation analysis, and no PGR variation.

missing.what: Naive-FT student versus weak-supervisor accuracy or content values, needed for V1 and for any PGR computation.
Explanation-technique (analogy) task results for naive FT versus weak model; no row records them.
Naive-FT and weak-model scores in the Table 1 setting, needed to judge bootstrap and the auxiliary-loss proxy against naive training.
Theoretical lower bound on naive weak-label fine-tuning risk (Prop. 3.2).

record.verdict_notes: The record's 'absent' and 'challenges' verdicts on V1 misread the authors' 'fails to achieve weak-to-strong generalization'. That phrase is against their own stricter baseline (the un-finetuned strong model), so it does not bear on beating the weak supervisor. Persona experiments instruct weak models to adopt the persona, but the strong student is not instructed, so these remain weak-supervision tests. The gender-bias experiment correctly stays excluded: its labels are GPT-corrupted, not from a weaker model.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not calculate PGR. It tests naive weak-label fine-tuning using task accuracy and explicitly reports that it fails to achieve weak-to-strong generalization in the stated GPT-3.5 math settings.
It evaluates bootstrapping and a data-doubling proxy for auxiliary confidence loss, but does not report PGR or a numeric naive-fine-tuning comparison for these methods.
It varies task, strong-model checkpoint, weak-label provider and weak-label quality. It does not systematically sweep model sizes or analyze representations.
No direct test of exploiting what a weak supervisor cannot check, distribution shift, or correlated weak/strong errors.
The theory concerns excess risk and refinement under transfer-learning assumptions; it does not establish conditions requiring a student to beat its supervisor.
No vision or other non-language experiment.

relationships.condition: GPT-4o-mini, persona task (tinyTruthfulQA and tinyAlpacaEval), bootstrapping (weak to GPT-3.5 to GPT-4o-mini) and a data-doubling auxiliary-loss proxy
relationships.reason: Text-based: bootstrapping 'still allows for too much corruption'. The proxy raises content but cuts style (style 2.38-5.65; tb33-tb48). Bootstrap content is 2.88-5.29 on TruthfulQA (tb17-tb32). There is no naive baseline in Table 1.
relationships.display_finding: Bootstrapping retained substantial corruption, with TruthfulQA content scores of 2.88–5.29; the auxiliary-loss proxy improved content while reducing style, whose scores ranged from 2.38 to 5.65.

source_check.condition: GPT-4o-mini, persona task (tinyTruthfulQA and tinyAlpacaEval), bootstrapping (weak to GPT-3.5 to GPT-4o-mini) and a data-doubling auxiliary-loss proxy
source_check.reason: Section 5.1 gives qualitative support for accuracy improvements from both changes. Remaining corruption relative to the unchanged strong model and reduced style transfer do not contradict V2's improvement over naive training. PGR and numerical improvements over naive FT are not supplied.

relationships.condition: Linear mixture-of-regressions transfer framework with biased or noisy weak supervision
relationships.reason: Text-based (no rows). Prop. 3.2 shows naive fine-tuning's risk is bounded below by weak and source biases, so its gain is limited. The authors say this contrasts with Charikar, Lang and Wu.
relationships.display_finding: Naive fine-tuning retains risk floors from weak and source biases under biased supervision, while noisy supervision incurs an efficiency limitation and is unbiased at η = 0.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Linear mixture-of-regressions transfer framework with biased or noisy weak supervision
source_check.reason: Retain the label for the biased-supervision limitation, but narrow the bias-floor condition to biased weak supervision. Proposition 3.2 does not establish that floor for noisy supervision; the noisy estimator is unbiased at eta=0 and instead has an efficiency limitation.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.condition: GPT-4o-mini, persona task (tinyTruthfulQA and tinyAlpacaEval), bootstrapping (weak to GPT-3.5 to GPT-4o-mini) and a data-doubling auxiliary-loss proxy
labels.reason: Section 5.1 gives qualitative support for accuracy improvements from both changes. Remaining corruption relative to the unchanged strong model and reduced style transfer do not contradict V2's improvement over naive training. PGR and numerical improvements over naive FT are not supplied.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.condition: Linear mixture-of-regressions transfer framework with biased or noisy weak supervision
labels.reason: Retain the label for the biased-supervision limitation, but narrow the bias-floor condition to biased weak supervision. Proposition 3.2 does not establish that floor for noisy supervision; the noisy estimator is unbiased at eta=0 and instead has an efficiency limitation.

relation.reason: It provides its own theoretical results and weak-supervision experiments bearing on the claim.

tranche.reason: The paper explicitly argues for restating success relative to the unchanged strong model and gives theoretical and empirical limitations of naive weak-label training.

source_check.notes: Table 1 names Gemma 2b, whereas Section 5 names Gemma-1.2B. Theorem 4.3 separately supplies positive refinement guarantees under explicit structural and ICL assumptions.

statements.correction: Section 5.1: bootstrapping provides some safeguarding against accuracy degradation but leaves substantial corruption. Table 1: TruthfulQA content scores 3.79, 5.29, 3.12, 2.883; no naive-FT row; no reported PGR comparison.
statements.problem: The range and residual corruption are correctly reported, but they do not establish that bootstrapping fails to improve over naive fine-tuning. The paper explicitly reports some protection against degradation.

statements.correction: Table 1 has no naive-FT baseline. Section 5 and Figures 1–4 include naive-FT baselines. Section 5.1 reports partial protection from degradation through bootstrapping.
statements.problem: The corruption description is accurate, but the assertion that this study has no naive baseline is too broad.

statements.correction: Proposition 3.2: biased weak supervision; lower bound involving source and weak-model squared biases. Noisy supervision: estimator unbiased when eta=0, with poor asymptotic relative efficiency versus gold-label training. Sections 1.1 and 6 contrast the framework with Charikar, Lang and Wu.
statements.problem: Proposition 3.2's bias lower bound applies to biased weak supervision, not generally to the noisy case.

reader_labels.reason: The paper explicitly says naive weak-label fine-tuning fails to achieve weak-to-strong generalization in both datasets; see math35g and math35m.

reader_labels.reason: Naive fine-tuning substantially lowers GPT-3.5-Turbo's content score relative to its unchanged baseline, showing a capability cost; see p35a and p35t.
